quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
Once you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane first. Then slow down. Do not slow down before entering the exit lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Tow-away zone.
Steep downgrade.
Roadwork ahead.

questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign warns drivers to be careful when wet roads may be slippery.

questions.question: How should you position your front wheels when parking uphill on a street with a curb?

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if your brakes fail.

questions.question: If dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should slow down and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway angles toward the center. What does this mean?

options.text: There is an intersection just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You will be required to turn left just ahead.
The road will get narrower.

questions.explanation: Edge lines mark the boundary between the driving lane and shoulder. When an edge line angles toward the center, the road is narrowing.

questions.question: On multilane, one-way streets and highways, which lane should you use to turn left?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To better see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before trying to pass them.
Because following too closely will get you caught in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To better see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles block your view of the road ahead. Extra distance lets you see around them and spot road hazards early. Also, large vehicle drivers cannot see you directly behind them.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow in a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Is never used as a traffic signal.
Has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light.
Means that drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.
Tells drivers that a green arrow is about to be shown.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same as a yellow light. Slow down and prepare to stop.

questions.question: Before turning left, what is important to do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Yield to oncoming vehicles.
Swing to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go first.

questions.question: What is the best way to merge onto a freeway?

options.text: Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.
Accelerate to a speed that is faster than the speed of traffic.
Turn on your hazard lights until safely on the freeway.
Accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic. This lets you merge smoothly and safely. Vehicles entering the freeway must yield to traffic already on it.

questions.question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, what should a driver do?

options.text: Keep your speed and go through.
Stop, look both ways, and then proceed.
Let all other drivers go first.
Be ready to yield if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield if needed.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no stop sign or traffic light, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be ready to yield to prevent crashes. Do this by easing off the gas, covering the brake, and looking left, right, and left again.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive in bad conditions.
The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive in good conditions.
The suggested speed to drive in good conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive in good conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed you can drive in good conditions. You can drive slower than the posted limit, but you cannot drive faster. You must drive slower in school zones or work zones. If weather or road conditions make the posted speed unsafe, drive slower.

questions.question: How do you make room for cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Switch to a different lane.
Keep your speed and stay in your lane.

questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering a freeway. If you can, change to the next lane to create a gap for incoming vehicles. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to let vehicles enter safely.

questions.question: What does a solid white line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Lanes go opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Lanes go opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Lanes go the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Lanes go the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes go the same direction and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: You cannot drive faster than:

options.text: The posted speed limit.
A speed that is reasonable and safe.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not drive faster than what is reasonable and safe. Choose your speed based on the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road condition, and light. Always stay within legal speed limits.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must keep roads safe. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: You are crossing an intersection and see an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop right there in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right at the edge of the intersection and stop.
Finish crossing, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and/or sirens, finish crossing and then drive to the right and stop. Always yield to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Lane ends.
No right turn.
Slippery when wet.
Two-way traffic.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow and black and alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a lane is ending and drivers should prepare for traffic to merge.

questions.question: If a HAWK crosswalk light is black, what does it mean?

options.text: Drivers may go forward slowly.
Drivers should slow down and get ready to stop.
Drivers must stop completely.
There are no people crossing nearby.

questions.explanation: HAWK signals control pedestrian crossings. When the lights turn black, drivers can proceed through the crosswalk, but they should be careful.

questions.question: Use high beam headlights when driving in fog.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and can get in your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop completely. Then proceed when the road is clear.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on all of the following except:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, the time between drinks, and your weight. Physical fitness does not affect BAC.

questions.question: A steady yellow light is showing at an intersection ahead. You have not entered yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass through before it turns red.
Slow down and carefully go through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.explanation: When you see a steady yellow light and have not entered the intersection, stop safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: This road sign shows:

options.text: The safe speed limit for residential areas.
The safe speed for leaving a highway.
The safe speed for entering a highway.
The safe speed in a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The safe speed for leaving a highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the recommended safe speed for a highway exit. In this example, it is 30 mph.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrians may cross here.
Construction workers on or near the road.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow. This sign warns that people may be crossing the road ahead.

questions.question: Highway signs that tell drivers what they must do are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. Not following them is against the law.

questions.question: A car suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and brake hard.
Let off the gas pedal.
Swerve to the next lane.

questions.explanation: If a car cuts in front of you, release the gas pedal. This creates space between you and the other car without forcing you to brake hard or swerve.

questions.question: The best way to avoid danger while driving is to:

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always watch what is happening around your vehicle in front, on the sides, and behind you. This helps you see problems early so you can change speed or position safely.

questions.question: When parking uphill by a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill by a curb, turn your wheel away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will roll toward the curb and stop.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand point downward. What does this mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start moving.

questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point down, they are signaling that they will stop. Be ready to slow down or stop if you see this signal.
